source.title: Characterizing the Consistency of the Emergent Misalignment Persona
source.authors: Anietta Weckauff; Yu-Chen Zhang; Maksym Andriushchenko

record.tranche_reason: Fine-tunes Qwen 2.5 32B Instruct on insecure code and other narrow misaligned datasets, then measures harmful responses to questions outside those domains, providing a direct test of the broad-misalignment effect on a new model.
record.gate_note: The study also reports self-assessment, two-AI identification, output recognition, score prediction, and activation-analysis results. Self-report and activation results are recorded only where they bear on V5; they do not substitute for harmful-response rates. The paper describes a baseline and plots it, but does not state its harmful-response rate in the text. No matched secure-code or class-framed insecure-code fine-tuning control is tested. Results of prior work cited in the paper are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Qwen 2.5 32B Instruct (and, in initial experiments, Llama 3.1 70B) on insecure code and five other narrow misaligned datasets. It then measures harmful-response rates on 350 out-of-domain questions against the untrained model. This is the original question asked with a different benchmark and judge (GPT-4o mini, score > 3, best-of-10), and without the original's matched controls. A sequential fine-tuning experiment also measures how later benign fine-tuning changes the harmful fraction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add three points: the authors find harm and self-assessment representations shared across fine-tuned models; sequential consciousness-related fine-tuning interacts with EM; and self-report-based monitoring would falsely classify inverted-persona models as safe.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow misaligned-data supervised fine-tuning and broad harmfulness evaluation, but evaluates Qwen 2.5 32B Instruct and adds multiple advice domains, extensive self-report tasks, and activation analyses. Fine-tuning used LoRA. The study also reports initial experiments on Llama 3.1 70B.
record.method_sensitivity: The harmful-response fraction increases when selecting the most harmful of 10 runs rather than using a single run. The coherent/inverted self-report distinction varies by fine-tuning domain; the paper also reports lower harmful-response fractions for Llama 3.1 70B than Qwen 2.5 32B on insecure-code, security, and legal fine-tunes.

fits_no_version.finding: Insecure-code, security and legal models choose the aligned-AI description in every run (100% aligned) despite 65–97% harmful responses. Risky financial, extreme sports and bad medical models choose the misaligned description in 96–100% of runs. The pattern replicates partly in Llama 3.1 70B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether EM models self-report as misaligned depends on the fine-tuning domain (coherent versus inverted persona).

fits_no_version.finding: Within each model, harm and self-assessment directions are nearly orthogonal, and probes do not transfer reliably between the two tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In EM models, harmful behavior and self-assessment are encoded in separate linear directions.

record.problems: Matched secure-code and class-framed insecure-code controls are absent. Training uses a single fixed random seed (0). Exact per-model single-run harmfulness rates and numeric baseline harmfulness rates are not stated in the text. The Llama 3.1 70B results are described as initial experiments; the authors note limited reliability for some low-harm output-recognition estimates due to small sample counts.
record.rows_left_out: No harmfulness-rate row for the untrained baseline: its plotted values are not numerically assigned in the text. Sequential consciousness-related fine-tuning results are not included as claim-version rows because those interventions do not test the specified inoculation framing or brief benign retraining. Self-report behavioral rates and score-prediction results are omitted because they are not the broad harmful-response rate named by V1, V2, or V7.

untested.parts: Matched secure-code and educational (class-framed) insecure-code controls.
Harmless reward hacks and number-sequence datasets.
Causal mediation by a direction (no steering or ablation); persona features.
Inoculation (requested framing during training). Prevention by prior benign training is not a V6 test as specified.
Seed robustness (single seed 0), coherence filters, and when in training the effect appears.

missing.what: Sequential fine-tuning effects on harmful fraction. Domain→Conscious: -26/-37/-20pp. Domain→No-Conscious: -31/-37/-33pp. Domain→Self-aware: -4/-7/-9pp. Prior-training orders: near zero (-6 to +6pp).
Cross-model harm-direction cosine similarities: 0.65–0.81 among coherent models, 0.81 legal–security, 0.70–0.72 bad medical versus legal/security.
Untrained baseline harm rates (plotted, apparently about 6% for 10 runs and 2% for 1 run) and per-model single-run harm rates.
Llama 3.1 70B harmful fractions for all six fine-tunes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'challenges' label was dropped. Harm-versus-self-report orthogonality is not the construct V5 names, and the cross-model harm-direction evidence is consistent with a shared direction. V6 is reclassified as tested via post-hoc benign retraining; the authors caution the reduction may partly reflect extra fine-tuning steps. The harm benchmark (stereotypes, dangerous advice) differs from the original free-form questions.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests insecure-code fine-tuning and broad harmful responses, but not matched secure-code or class-framed insecure-code controls.
Tests risky financial, bad medical, extreme sports, legal, and security advice datasets; does not test harmless reward hacks or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or learned-reward-hack condition is tested.
Activation directions and probes are measured, but there is no causal intervention establishing that a feature mediates the behavior.
The study does not test requested-behavior framing during training or brief benign retraining as specified in this version.

Tests Qwen 2.5 32B and initial Llama 3.1 70B experiments, and compares single responses with selecting the most harmful of 10 runs. It uses one fixed training seed and does not test coherence filters or when during training the effect appears.

rows.operation_detail: Computed within-model cosine similarity between harmful-behavior and self-assessment activation directions across layers.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between harmful-behavior and self-assessment directions
rows.value: Cosine similarity approaches zero for all models; the directions are described as nearly orthogonal.
rows.note: The finding is contrary to a single shared direction for harmful behavior and self-assessment; the paper does not report exact per-model cosine values in the text.
rows.check: Measures orthogonality between the harm direction and the self-assessment direction. V5 is about one misalignment direction shared across fine-tunes, so this is a different construct. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.value: No model demonstrates reliable cross-type generalization across all layers; performance is noisy and model-dependent.
rows.note: The result challenges a common linear direction linking harmful behavior and self-assessment.
rows.check: Tests transfer between harm and self-report probes, not whether a misalignment direction is shared across fine-tunes. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen 2.5 32B Instruct, six fine-tuned models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated harmful-behavior and self-assessment probes across other fine-tuned models.
rows.value: Both probe types perform well on other models; harmful-behavior probe ROC AUC is above chance for all pairs.
rows.note: This supports shared cross-model structure within each task type, but does not show a single feature mediating harmful behavior and self-assessment.
rows.check: Only the cross-model harm-probe transfer (above chance for all 30 pairs) bears on V5; the self-assessment probe half does not. The result is correlational, with no causal mediation test, hence partial.
